subsystems.name: Electroactive polymer active layer
subsystems.role: changes shape or stiffness when an electric field is applied, providing the actuation.

subsystems.name: Compliant electrodes
subsystems.role: deliver the electric field across the active layer without restricting its deformation.

subsystems.name: Variable stiffness mechanism
subsystems.role: mimics fascia by allowing the actuator to switch between soft and rigid states.

subsystems.name: Sensing and feedback layer
subsystems.role: provides tactile and position feedback for closed-loop control.

subsystems.name: Encapsulation and insulation
subsystems.role: protects the actuator from moisture and prevents electrical breakdown.

subsystems.name: Drive and control electronics
subsystems.role: supplies the high voltage and control signals needed to operate the actuator.

buildSteps.title: Design and model the actuator
buildSteps.detail: Choose the EAP material and geometry, and simulate the electromechanical response, stiffness range and force output for the intended prosthetic or surgical application.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the active film
buildSteps.detail: Cast or synthesize the dielectric elastomer or ionic polymer film to the required thickness and uniformity, then cure it.

buildSteps.title: Apply compliant electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Deposit conductive material such as carbon grease or a stretchable conductive elastomer on both faces of the film, ensuring it remains conductive under large strains.

buildSteps.title: Build the variable stiffness layer
buildSteps.detail: Stack jamming layers or shape memory elements that can be locked and unlocked to change stiffness, mimicking fascia.

buildSteps.title: Integrate sensing and encapsulation
buildSteps.detail: Laminate strain and pressure sensors into the stack, then encapsulate the whole actuator in a flexible, insulating coating to prevent electrical breakdown and protect against moisture.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and wire the device
buildSteps.detail: Connect electrical leads to the electrodes and any fluidic lines for jamming, then integrate the actuator into a prosthetic socket or surgical tool.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Measure actuation strain, blocking force, stiffness change, response time and cycle life; calibrate the control system for safe and precise operation.

prerequisites.why: EAPs can deform by tens of percent, but many suffer from fatigue, require high driving voltages, and have limited lifetime.
Electrodes must maintain conductivity while stretching with the polymer; current solutions degrade over time.
Many EAPs need kilovolt-level driving voltages, but compact, safe power electronics are still bulky or inefficient.
For prosthetics and surgery, materials must be non-toxic, resist bodily fluids, and survive sterilization.
Integrating soft sensors with control algorithms to achieve natural, stable feedback remains a research challenge.

pathway.milestone: Lab prototypes of EAP actuators demonstrate basic bending, contraction and variable stiffness.
pathway.unlocks: Proof that soft artificial muscles can mimic some muscle functions.

pathway.milestone: Integrated soft actuators with tactile sensing and adjustable stiffness are tested in prosthetic hands and surgical grippers, including clinical trials.
pathway.unlocks: Devices that can safely and gently interact with humans and delicate tissues.

pathway.milestone: First commercial prosthetic limbs and surgical instruments using soft actuators reach the market.
pathway.unlocks: More natural feel and control for amputees, and less invasive surgery.

pathway.milestone: Fully soft robotic systems with distributed actuation, sensing and variable stiffness, closely mimicking human muscles and fascia, become common.
pathway.unlocks: Advanced prosthetics, versatile surgical robots, and safer human-robot collaboration.
